name: Greater London Ultra Low Emission Zone (ULEZ)
operatingHours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, every day of the year (except Christmas Day 25 December)
enforcementMethod: Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras across all Greater London borders
pcnRule: PCN is £180, reduced to £90 if paid within 14 days. Must be paid by midnight on the third day following travel.

standards.petrol: Euro 4 (NOx) - Generally vehicles registered with the DVLA after 1 January 2006
standards.diesel: Euro 6 (NOx and PM) - Generally vehicles registered after 1 September 2015 (65 plate)
standards.electric: 100% Zero-emission vehicles (Battery Electric & Hydrogen Fuel Cell) are completely exempt (£0)
standards.hybrid: Must meet relevant Euro standard (Euro 4 for petrol-hybrid, Euro 6 for diesel-hybrid)

summary: The London ULEZ covers all 32 London boroughs and the City of London up to the administrative boundary. Non-compliant vehicles must pay £12.50 daily.
description: The Ultra Low Emission Zone (ULEZ) operates across all Greater London boroughs to help clean up London's air. If your vehicle doesn't meet the strict ULEZ emission standards and isn't exempt, you need to pay a daily charge of £12.50 to drive within the zone. The zone operates 24/7 every day of the year, except Christmas Day.
exemptions: Wheelchair accessible PHVs and designated disabled tax class vehicles (grace period to 2027)
Historic vehicles registered with DVLA under the 'historic tax class' (built before 1 January 1984 / 40+ years old)
NHS patient reimbursement for clinically vulnerable patients attending hospital

vehicleCharges.notes: Free if Euro 6 or newer (post-Sept 2015 / 65 plate)
Covered by London LEZ standards (Euro VI required)

paymentWindow: Pay in advance, on the day of travel, or up to midnight on the third day after travel

faqs.question: Does the London ULEZ apply 24 hours a day?
faqs.answer: Yes, the ULEZ operates 24 hours a day, midnight to midnight, 7 days a week, every day of the year except Christmas Day (25 December).

faqs.question: What happens if I cross the ULEZ boundary after midnight?
faqs.answer: The charging period runs from midnight to midnight. If you drive within the ULEZ across midnight (e.g. 23:45 to 00:30), you will need to pay two daily charges (£25.00 total) if your vehicle is non-compliant.

faqs.question: How do I check if my car is Euro 4 or Euro 6?
faqs.answer: You can use our vehicle checker above, or look at section V.5 of your vehicle's V5C logbook, which lists the exact Euro emission standard.

faqs.question: Are residents inside the ULEZ exempt from the charge?
faqs.answer: No. There are no general resident exemptions or discounts for living inside the Greater London ULEZ. If your vehicle does not meet the standards, you must pay the £12.50 daily fee whenever you drive it on public roads.

name: London Congestion Charge
operatingHours: 07:00 to 18:00 Monday to Friday; 12:00 to 18:00 Saturday, Sunday and Bank Holidays (no charge between Christmas Day and New Year's Day bank holiday inclusive)
enforcementMethod: High-density ANPR camera ring around Central London
pcnRule: PCN is £180, halved to £90 if paid within 14 days. Must pay by midnight on the third day (£17.50 if paying after day of travel).

standards.petrol: Standard £15 daily fee applies regardless of Euro emission standard
standards.diesel: Standard £15 daily fee applies regardless of Euro emission standard
standards.electric: Cleaner Vehicle Discount: 100% discount for registered zero-emission vehicles (£10/year TfL registration)
standards.hybrid: Plugin-hybrids are no longer exempt; must pay full £15 daily rate
standards.motorcycle: Two-wheeled motorbikes and mopeds are completely exempt (£0)

summary: Central London traffic reduction charge of £15/day covering Soho, the City, Westminster, and Southwark during operating hours.
description: The London Congestion Charge is an 8-square-mile zone in Central London designed to reduce traffic congestion and air pollution. Unlike ULEZ (which is 24/7 and emissions-based), the Congestion Charge applies to almost all combustion-engine vehicles entering the zone during peak daytime hours.
exemptions: Zero-emission battery electric vehicles registered with TfL under the Cleaner Vehicle Discount
Two-wheeled motorcycles, mopeds and pedal bicycles
Blue Badge holders (100% discount upon TfL registration)
Residents within the Congestion Charge zone get a 90% discount with an active permit

vehicleCharges.notes: Applies during charging hours regardless of Euro standard
Applies during charging hours regardless of Euro standard
100% discount with TfL registration (ends Dec 2025/2026 reform)
Standard commercial vans must pay full rate

paymentWindow: Pay in advance or on the day for £15; pay up to the third day after travel for £17.50

faqs.question: Is the Congestion Charge separate from ULEZ?
faqs.answer: Yes. They are two separate schemes. If you drive a non-compliant vehicle in Central London during Congestion Charge hours, you must pay both the £12.50 ULEZ fee AND the £15.00 Congestion Charge fee (£27.50 total per day).

faqs.question: What are the exact Congestion Charge operating hours?
faqs.answer: Monday to Friday: 07:00 – 18:00. Saturday, Sunday and Bank Holidays: 12:00 – 18:00. Outside these hours, driving in Central London is free from Congestion Charge (though ULEZ still applies 24/7).

name: Birmingham Clean Air Zone (Class D)
operatingHours: 24 hours a day, 365 days a year
enforcementMethod: Over 67 ANPR camera sites across the A4540 Middleway ring road boundary
pcnRule: PCN is £120, reduced to £60 if paid within 14 days. Must be paid within 6 days following the day of travel.

standards.hybrid: Petrol hybrids Euro 4+; diesel hybrids Euro 6+
standards.motorcycle: All mopeds and motorcycles are exempt (£0)

summary: Birmingham Class D CAZ covers all roads inside the A4540 Middleway ring road. Non-compliant cars & vans pay £8/day.
description: Birmingham's Clean Air Zone (Class D) covers all roads inside the A4540 Middleway ring road (the ring road itself is not charged). It operates 24/7 all year round. Vehicles that do not meet Euro 4 (petrol) or Euro 6 (diesel) standards must pay a daily charge of £8 (cars and LGVs) or £50 (HGVs, buses and coaches).
exemptions: Disabled passenger tax class and Blue Badge holder vehicles registered locally
Historic vehicles (tax class 'historic vehicle', over 40 years old)
Specialist emergency vehicles and community transport
Pure electric vehicles and hydrogen fuel cell vehicles

vehicleCharges.notes: Applies to non-compliant commercial light vehicles

paymentWindow: Pay 6 days before travel, on the day, or up to 6 days after travel

faqs.question: Can I drive on the Birmingham Middleway ring road without paying?
faqs.answer: Yes! The A4540 Middleway ring road itself is not part of the Clean Air Zone. You only incur a charge if you turn off the ring road into the city centre zone.

faqs.question: Where do I pay the Birmingham Clean Air Zone charge?
faqs.answer: Payments must be made through the official central UK Government Clean Air Zone payment service at gov.uk/clean-air-zones.

name: Bristol Clean Air Zone (Class D)
operatingHours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year
enforcementMethod: ANPR cameras across central Bristol and Portway access corridor
pcnRule: PCN is £120, reduced to £60 if paid within 14 days. Must be paid within 6 days after travel.

standards.hybrid: Petrol hybrids Euro 4+; diesel hybrids Euro 6+
standards.motorcycle: All motorcycles and mopeds are exempt (£0)

summary: Bristol Class D CAZ covers central Bristol, Cumberland Basin, and the Portway. Non-compliant cars & vans pay £9/day.
description: Bristol's Clean Air Zone operates 24/7 across the city centre, parts of Redcliffe, Clifton, and the Portway (A4). Like Birmingham, Bristol is a Class D zone, meaning private passenger cars that do not meet emissions standards are charged £9 per day.
exemptions: Disabled tax class and registered blue badge exemptions (local registration required)
paymentWindow: Pay up to 6 days before, on the day, or up to 6 days after travel

faqs.question: Does the Bristol CAZ cover the Portway and Brunel Way?
faqs.answer: Yes, sections of the Portway (A4) and Cumberland Basin / Brunel Way are included in the Bristol CAZ. If your vehicle is non-compliant, you will trigger the £9 charge.

faqs.question: How long do I have to pay the Bristol CAZ charge?
faqs.answer: You have 6 days after your journey to make the payment via gov.uk/clean-air-zones.

name: Bath Clean Air Zone (Class C)
operatingHours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year
enforcementMethod: ANPR cameras on all arterial approaches to Bath city centre
pcnRule: PCN is £120, reduced to £60 if paid within 14 days. Must pay within 6 days of travel.

standards.petrol: Euro 4 (applicable to commercial vans, taxis, and HGVs only)
standards.diesel: Euro 6 (applicable to commercial vans, taxis, and HGVs only)
standards.hybrid: Follows relevant Euro standard for commercial vehicles
standards.motorcycle: All private cars and motorcycles are exempt

summary: Bath Class C CAZ charges non-compliant commercial vans, taxis, and HGVs. Private passenger cars are completely EXEMPT.
description: Bath operates a Class C Clean Air Zone. A major advantage for motorists: PRIVATE PASSENGER CARS AND MOTORCYCLES ARE COMPLETELY EXEMPT (£0), regardless of fuel type or age. Only commercial vehicles (taxis, private hire, vans, LGVs, buses, coaches, and HGVs) that do not meet Euro 6 (diesel) or Euro 4 (petrol) standards are charged.
exemptions: ALL PRIVATE PASSENGER CARS (Euro standards do not apply to private non-commercial cars)

vehicleCharges.notes: 100% exempt from Bath CAZ regardless of age/fuel

paymentWindow: Pay within 6 days after driving in the zone

faqs.question: Do I have to pay in Bath if I drive a private car?
faqs.answer: No. Bath operates a Class C Clean Air Zone, meaning all private passenger cars are completely exempt from the charge, regardless of age, fuel type or emissions standard.

faqs.question: What vehicles have to pay the Bath Clean Air Zone charge?
faqs.answer: Only non-compliant taxis, private hire vehicles, commercial vans, minibuses, buses, coaches, and HGVs are subject to charges in Bath.

name: Sheffield Clean Air Zone (Class C)
operatingHours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year
enforcementMethod: ANPR cameras monitoring Sheffield Inner Ring Road (A61) and city centre
pcnRule: PCN is £120, reduced to £60 if paid within 14 days. Must pay within 6 days of travel.

standards.hybrid: Follows relevant Euro standard for commercial vehicles
standards.motorcycle: All private cars and motorcycles are exempt

summary: Sheffield Class C CAZ charges non-compliant commercial vans (£10/day) and HGVs (£50/day). Private cars are EXEMPT.
description: Sheffield's Clean Air Zone is Class C, covering the Inner Ring Road (A61) and the city centre, extending up the Sheffield Parkway to the roundabout at Prince of Wales Road. Private passenger cars and motorbikes are completely EXEMPT from all charges.
exemptions: ALL PRIVATE PASSENGER CARS AND MOTORCYCLES
Fully electric and hydrogen commercial vehicles
paymentWindow: Pay up to 6 days before, on the day, or up to 6 days after travel

faqs.question: Are private cars charged in the Sheffield Clean Air Zone?
faqs.answer: No. Private cars and motorbikes never pay in Sheffield. Only older, higher-polluting commercial vehicles (vans, LGVs, taxis, buses, coaches, and HGVs) are charged.

name: Newcastle & Gateshead (Tyneside) Clean Air Zone (Class C)
operatingHours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year
enforcementMethod: ANPR cameras monitoring city centre and Tyne Bridge corridor
pcnRule: PCN is £120, reduced to £60 if paid within 14 days.

standards.hybrid: Follows relevant Euro standard for commercial vehicles
standards.motorcycle: All private cars and motorcycles are exempt

summary: Newcastle & Gateshead Class C CAZ charges non-compliant commercial vans (£12.50/day) and HGVs (£50/day). Private cars are EXEMPT.
description: The Tyneside Clean Air Zone covers Newcastle city centre, routes over the Tyne, Swing, High Level and Redheugh bridges. Private cars and motorbikes are EXEMPT. Non-compliant commercial vans, LGVs and taxis pay £12.50 per day, while HGVs, buses and coaches pay £50.
exemptions: ALL PRIVATE PASSENGER CARS AND MOTORCYCLES
paymentWindow: Pay within 6 days after travel via gov.uk

faqs.question: Does the Tyne Bridge have Clean Air Zone cameras?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Tyne Bridge approach is part of the Newcastle & Gateshead Clean Air Zone. However, private passenger cars are exempt and will not be charged.

operatingHours: 24 hours a day, 365 days a year
enforcementMethod: Over 300 ANPR cameras covering inner ring road and Shipley corridor
pcnRule: PCN is £120, reduced to £60 if paid within 14 days.

standards.hybrid: Follows relevant Euro standard for commercial vehicles

description: The Bradford Clean Air Zone is a Class C+ zone covering the Bradford outer ring road, city centre, Canal Road, Manningham Lane, and Shipley / Saltaire. Private cars and motorbikes are completely EXEMPT.
exemptions: ALL PRIVATE PASSENGER CARS AND MOTORCYCLES
Local business exemptions (subject to council permit)
paymentWindow: Pay up to 6 days before or 6 days after travel

faqs.question: Do private residents pay the Bradford CAZ fee?
faqs.answer: No, private cars are never charged in Bradford. Only commercial vehicles, vans, minibuses, HGVs, and taxis must comply.

name: Portsmouth Clean Air Zone (Class B)
operatingHours: 24 hours a day, 365 days a year
enforcementMethod: ANPR cameras across southwest Portsea Island
pcnRule: PCN is £120, reduced to £60 if paid within 14 days.

standards.hybrid: Follows relevant Euro standard for commercial vehicles
standards.motorcycle: All private cars, private vans, and motorcycles are exempt

summary: Portsmouth Class B CAZ charges non-compliant taxis (£10/day) and HGVs/buses (£50/day). ALL private cars and private vans are EXEMPT.
description: Portsmouth operates a Class B Clean Air Zone covering southwest Portsea Island (including Kingston Crescent, Fratton, and city centre). As a Class B zone, private passenger cars AND private commercial vans are completely EXEMPT from all charges.
exemptions: ALL STANDARD PRIVATE VANS AND LGVs

vehicleCharges.notes: Class B CAZ exempts standard vans
Non-compliant HGVs, buses and coaches pay £50/day

paymentWindow: Pay up to 6 days before or 6 days after travel via gov.uk

faqs.question: Do vans pay the Portsmouth Clean Air Zone charge?
faqs.answer: No! Portsmouth is a Class B zone, which means private cars and standard vans are exempt. Only taxis, private hire vehicles, HGVs, and buses/coaches are charged.

name: Oxford Zero Emission Zone (ZEZ Pilot)
operatingHours: 07:00 to 19:00, 7 days a week, 365 days a year
enforcementMethod: ANPR cameras monitoring designated central streets
pcnRule: PCN is £60, reduced to £30 if paid within 14 days.
unverifiedFields: Exact future date for full city-wide ZEZ expansion beyond the pilot streets

standards.petrol: Non-EV petrol vehicles must pay the daily emission fee (£10/day)
standards.diesel: Non-EV diesel vehicles must pay the daily emission fee (£10/day)
standards.electric: 100% zero-emission battery electric vehicles (EVs) are completely free (£0)
standards.hybrid: Ultra-low emission hybrids (emissions <75g/km) pay £2 - £4; standard hybrids pay £10
standards.motorcycle: Zero-emission electric motorbikes free; petrol bikes pay £2 - £10

summary: Oxford ZEZ is the UK's first Zero Emission Zone. 100% electric vehicles are free; all combustion engine vehicles pay £2–£10/day.
description: The Oxford Zero Emission Zone (ZEZ) pilot operates across central Oxford streets (including Cornmarket, Queen St, Bonn Square, St Michael's St, and Ship St) from 07:00 to 19:00 daily. Only 100% zero-emission vehicles (pure electric cars and hydrogen) can drive for free. All petrol, diesel, and non-exempt hybrid vehicles must pay a daily charge.
exemptions: 100% Zero-emission electric vehicles and hydrogen fuel cell vehicles
Registered blue badge holders (100% discount upon council registration)
Designated emergency service and recovery vehicles
Residents within the ZEZ pilot area receive a 90% discount

vehicleCharges.notes: Tiered rate based on CO2 and electric range

paymentWindow: Pay up to 6 days before or up to 6 days after the date of travel

faqs.question: Can I drive in Oxford without paying if my car is Euro 6?
faqs.answer: In the ZEZ pilot streets, even Euro 6 petrol and diesel cars must pay £10. Only 100% pure electric vehicles enter free of charge.

name: Glasgow Low Emission Zone (LEZ)
operatingHours: 24 hours a day, 365 days a year
enforcementMethod: ANPR camera enforcement across all city centre entry points
pcnRule: PCN is £60 (halved to £30 if paid within 14 days). Penalty doubles for each subsequent breach within 90 days: £120, £240, up to £480 cap for cars/vans, £960 for HGVs.

standards.hybrid: Petrol hybrids Euro 4+; diesel hybrids Euro 6+
standards.motorcycle: All two-wheeled mopeds and motorbikes are exempt

summary: Glasgow LEZ enforces a strict ban on non-compliant vehicles with NO daily pay option. Automatic £60 fine issued (doubling up to £480).
description: Unlike English Clean Air Zones and London ULEZ, Scottish Low Emission Zones HAVE NO DAILY CHARGE OPTION. Non-compliant vehicles are legally banned from entering Glasgow City Centre (bounded by the M8 motorway and the River Clyde). Drivers of non-compliant vehicles entering the zone receive an automatic statutory Penalty Charge Notice (PCN) of £60, which doubles on each subsequent breach up to £480 for cars/vans.
exemptions: Blue Badge holders (national exemption across all Scottish LEZs - must register beforehand)
Historic vehicles over 30 years old (not used for commercial purposes)
paymentWindow: No daily pass exists. If issued a PCN, pay within 14 days for 50% discount

faqs.question: Can I pay a daily fee to drive a non-compliant car in Glasgow?
faqs.answer: NO. Scottish LEZs have no daily charge option. You cannot pay £12.50 or any other fee to enter. Non-compliant vehicles are strictly banned and will receive an automatic fine.

faqs.question: Is the M8 motorway included in the Glasgow LEZ?
faqs.answer: No. The M8 motorway is excluded from the Glasgow LEZ. However, if you leave the M8 via an off-ramp into the city centre, you immediately enter the LEZ.

standards.hybrid: Petrol hybrids Euro 4+; diesel hybrids Euro 6+
standards.motorcycle: All motorcycles and mopeds are exempt

summary: Edinburgh LEZ covers the City Centre, Old Town and New Town. Non-compliant vehicles are banned (automatic £60 fine, no daily fee).
description: Enforcement for Edinburgh's Low Emission Zone began in June 2024. Covering 1.2 square miles of Edinburgh city centre from Queen Street to the Meadows, non-compliant vehicles are prohibited. Scottish LEZ legislation does not permit daily passes; any non-compliant vehicle detected receives an automatic £60 PCN.
exemptions: Blue Badge holders (national Scottish exemption - pre-registration required)
paymentWindow: No daily pass. PCN reduced to £30 if paid within 14 days

faqs.question: When did Edinburgh LEZ enforcement start?
faqs.answer: Enforcement in Edinburgh began on 1 June 2024 following a two-year grace period. All non-compliant vehicles are now actively fined.

faqs.question: Is the Dundee Marketgait ring road part of the LEZ?

faqs.question: When did Aberdeen LEZ enforcement begin?
faqs.answer: Aberdeen LEZ camera enforcement began on 1 June 2024. Non-compliant vehicles are subject to automatic £60 fines.
